CMP storm drain from Meadow Lark Dr. to channel at Mission Center Rd. needs to be repaired. It is failing and leaks water out at more than on spot on the hillside. As you can see in the picture it is adjacent to two high voltage transmission structures. The soil type on the hillside is a cobble and when any concentrated amount of water hits the hillside it easily erodes. We don't want to have a tower failure at this site due to the storm drain. It was patched in one area several years ago and the blockage at the bottom was cleared. However, it is leaking in other places uphill from the patch. we have installed BMPs to protect the towers but those are only temporary until the storm drain can be properly repaired. Due to the steepness and soil conditions this might be a prime candidate for relining. I must reiterate, there are four transmission circuits of critical importance to keeping the power on in San Diego. There are two 230kV, one 138kV and one 69kV on those two towers.
